title: Caveman hooks double-registered (plugin.json + manual copies in settings.json): every prompt and every session start injects duplicate context (~45k tokens wasted in main mega-run session alone)
mechanism: The caveman plugin registers SessionStart:caveman-activate.js and UserPromptSubmit:caveman-mode-tracker.js via its own plugin.json (enabledPlugins caveman@caveman=true at user level ~/.claude/settings.json:133 AND project .claude/settings.local.json). Additionally the same two scripts were manually copied to ~/.claude/hooks/ (files dated Apr 23, legacy install.sh path) and registered in ~/.claude/settings.json:85 (SessionStart) and :105 (UserPromptSubmit). Both registrations fire on every event. The kit git mirror kit/settings.example.json:85,105 bakes the same duplication in as ground truth.
evidence: Transcript 2a557a47 (fresh session 2026-07-02 11:17, exactly 1 user prompt): TWO identical hook_additional_context attachments 'CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full). Drop articles/filler...' (lines 16-17) and TWO SessionStart hook_success attachments each carrying the full 1215-byte ruleset 'CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full' (lines 3-4). Same 2x pattern in d61d6e5e (lines 3-4, 15-16). Counts: main mega-run session b8009145 = 1,349 per-prompt reminders + 146 session-start rulesets (halves redundant: ~674×35 tok + ~73×300 tok ≈ 45k tokens); current session 67b1586c = 100 + 6 (~2.9k tokens). Measured: caveman-activate.js stdout = 1,215 bytes; tracker per-prompt output = 203 bytes JSON (flag file ~/.claude/.caveman-active active). Waste compounds: each duplicate stays in history and is re-sent as input on every subsequent turn of the session.
why_weak: Pure token leak on the highest-frequency events (every user prompt + every session start/resume) with zero added function — the second injection is byte-identical to the first. Directly contradicts the kit's token-economy goal; none of the 5 known reports (UNIFIED-BACKLOG, error-taxonomy, kit-weakpoints, op-detect backlog, kit-upgrade-report) mention it.
proposed_direction: Delete the two manual caveman hook entries (SessionStart caveman-activate.js, UserPromptSubmit caveman-mode-tracker.js) from ~/.claude/settings.json AND kit/settings.example.json (keep statusLine — the plugin does not provide it; keep plugin registration as the single source). Verify: fresh session transcript must show exactly 1 'CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full)' per prompt and 1 ruleset per SessionStart. Also run kit-inventory/hook-test since settings.json is kit ground truth.

title: wiki-sa MCP (3659-doc Obsidian search) mounted user-globally, injected into every session of this project, used 0 times in 2.5 months
mechanism: wiki-sa is configured in global ~/.claude.json mcpServers ('/opt/homebrew/bin/qmd mcp') — user scope, so it connects in EVERY project including AI_Traiding_Bot, injecting its MCP instructions block at each session start.
evidence: grep '"name":"mcp__wiki-sa__' across all 12 project transcripts (incl. 126MB main mega-run session b8009145, Apr 19–Jul 2): 0 calls in every file. Measured injection: mcp_instructions_delta in 2a557a47 shows wiki-sa block = 1,275 bytes (~320 tokens) added at session start, every session including every scheduled auto-resume run. The server belongs to the Wiki-SA Obsidian project (projectPath '/Users/Apple/Documents/Obsidian Vault/Wiki-SA' per installed_plugins.json project-scope installs).
why_weak: Permanent per-session context tax (~320 tok × every session/resume) plus a qmd process spawn at each session start, for a search corpus that this project's cascade (wiki → mem-search → grep → read) never touches — the kit's own cascade rule makes it redundant here.
proposed_direction: Move wiki-sa out of global ~/.claude.json mcpServers into project scope of the Wiki-SA vault (e.g. .mcp.json there or claude mcp add --scope project executed in that directory). Verify next AI_Traiding_Bot session shows no wiki-sa in mcp_instructions_delta.

title: warp plugin enabled user-wide: 89,766 recorded hook invocations with zero possible function in the operator's desktop/scheduled environment
mechanism: warp@claude-code-warp (enabledPlugins true, ~/.claude/settings.json:136 area) registers hooks on 6 events including PostToolUse matcher '*' (every tool call) and UserPromptSubmit. Every invocation spawns bash, sources should-use-structured.sh, and exits early unless WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION env is set — which only happens inside Warp terminal. The operator works via Claude Code desktop and launchd-scheduled sessions (OQ-4: 'не пользуюсь claude CLI, работаю только через Claude Code desktop'), where Warp env vars are never present.
evidence: ~/.claude.json pluginUsage: warp@inline usageCount = 89,766 (lastUsedAt in current period) — i.e. ~90k hook process spawns that all hit the early-exit branch (should-use-structured.sh returns 1 when WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION unset; confirmed by reading scripts/should-use-structured.sh and on-post-tool-use.sh: 'if ! should_use_structured; then exit 0; fi'). Each spawn also writes a hook_success attachment line into the transcript (log noise). At ~20-50ms per spawn this is roughly 30-75 minutes of cumulative dead latency across the period, concentrated on the hottest path (after every tool call), with 0 tokens of benefit.
why_weak: Pure overhead in this environment: the plugin can only ever no-op outside Warp, yet it fires on every tool call and every prompt, including unattended auto-resume runs where latency directly burns limit-window time.
proposed_direction: Set warp@claude-code-warp: false in ~/.claude/settings.json enabledPlugins (and kit/settings.example.json mirror); re-enable only for sessions actually launched inside Warp. Verify via pluginUsage counter freeze and absence of warp hook_success attachments in a fresh transcript.

title: sqlite-trading and fetch MCP servers in committed .mcp.json are dead weight: 1 call in 2.5 months and 0 calls ever, respectively
mechanism: .mcp.json:1-14 spawns mcp-server-sqlite (uvx, --db-path data/bot.db) and mcp-server-fetch (uvx) at every interactive session start. fetch duplicates the built-in WebFetch tool; sqlite-trading duplicates what Bash+sqlite3 or direct file access covers, and the money core is frozen during kit-maintenance.
evidence: grep across all 12 transcripts: mcp__sqlite-trading__* called exactly once — list_tables at 2026-04-26T23:17:30Z (main session b8009145); mcp__fetch__fetch called 0 times in any transcript. Both servers connected at current session start (deferred_tools_delta 2026-07-01T21:11:38Z) — two uvx process spawns per session; in the deferred-tools harness their schema cost is near zero, but in vanilla CLI sessions ~6+1 tool schemas would load (~800 tok). Kit docs still count them as needed: CLAUDE.md navigation table advertises '8 MCP' and kit-audit-2026-04-27 concluded 'ALL components NEEDED, no removals' — contradicted by 1 use in 74 days.
why_weak: Session-start spawn cost and inventory drift for servers nobody uses; the '8 MCP / all needed' canon no longer reflects reality, which is exactly the count-drift class the kit already fights (KIT-006) but at the MCP layer.
proposed_direction: Remove fetch from .mcp.json (WebFetch covers it — note Sprint 32c added it, git log df521a6); keep sqlite-trading only if a concrete post-unfreeze use case exists, else drop and re-add when needed. Update tooling-inventory-ru MCP count via kit-inventory AUTO-block.
